question.problem:
Let $F(x)=4x-1$ for $x\in R.$ Suppose $f(x)$ is the $6$-periodic extension of $F(x)$ from $x\in [0,6)$ to $x\in R.$ Which of the following statements are true?

I. $f(x+12)=f(x)$ for all $x\in R$

II. $f(x)=F(x)$ for all $x\in R$

III. $f(x+3)=f(x)$ for all $x\in R$
question.worked_solution:
Since $f$ is the $6$-periodic extension of $F,$ we have 

- $f(x+6)=f(x)$ for all $x\in R,$ and

- $f(x)=F(x)$ for all $x\in [0,6).$

With that in mind, let's examine our statements in turn.

- Statement I is true. We have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x+12)=f((x+6)+6)=f(x+6)=f(x).\end{aligned}
$$

for all $x\in R.$

- Statement II is false. For example, take $x=7.$ Then,

$$
\begin{aligned}f(7)=f(1+6)=f(1)=F(1)=3,\end{aligned}
$$

while

$$
\begin{aligned}F(7)=27.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $f(x)\ne F(x)$ for $x=7.$

- Statement III is false. For example, take $x=2.$ Then,

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2+3)=f(5)=F(5)=19\end{aligned}
$$

while

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2)=F(2)=7.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $f(x+3)\ne f(x)$ for $x=2.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only".
